source.title: Sparse but not Simpler: A Multi-Level Interpretability Analysis of Vision Transformers

record.tranche_reason: The study compares dense and weight-pruned vision transformers and reports that pruning does not systematically reduce measured feature multiplexing or improve interpretability, qualifying the claim that sparsity promotes interpretable representations. It does not test the toy-model geometry directly.
record.gate_note: The study reports additional circuit-size, attribution, and SAE reconstruction outcomes. They are not rows for V2 because they do not directly measure feature sharing or polysemanticity. Circuit results are recorded under fits_no_version because they report structural circuit compactness and node use, which the listed versions do not specifically cover. The neuron ablation tail is also not a direct measure of V2's feature multiplexing claim.
record.test_reason: The study asks whether post-hoc weight pruning makes DeiT-III ViTs more interpretable. It takes superposition as background and uses SAEs and polysemanticity proxies as probes. None of its results bear on a listed version. It has no toy setting (V1). It never tests whether polysemanticity is caused by capacity competition (V2) or arises without capacity pressure (V3). Pruning removes weights, not neurons or dimensions. The model is a vision transformer, not an LLM (V4). It does not assess SAE completeness, stability or canonicity (V5), or feature dimensionality (V6). Its question is the effect of an intervention (weight sparsity) on polysemanticity proxies, which no version names.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Authors conclude that weight sparsity cuts circuit edges about 2.5× but not node usage. Neurons and SAE features stay highly polysemantic, so 'sparsity alone does not meaningfully reduce representational superposition'. They stress this rests on proxy measures. Attribution gains are modest and only at low sparsity.
record.recipe_differences: Uses post-hoc Wanda weight pruning followed by fine-tuning on DeiT-III B/16, with neuron, SAE, circuit, and attribution measurements. It does not reproduce the toy-model setup or method in Toy Models of Superposition.
record.method_sensitivity: Circuit extraction is sensitive to the sparsity penalty: for the Wanda 70% model, using the dense-model penalty produces lower circuit accuracy and higher variance than the selected lower penalty. The reported attribution metrics also vary with pruning level.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 0–70% Wanda pruning of DeiT-III B/16, neuron and block-11 SAE-feature selectivity, label entropy and class variance show no systematic change. Neurons 'remain similarly polysemantic'; 10% shows a non-persistent SAE shift.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-hoc weight pruning does not reduce neuron- or SAE-level polysemanticity proxies in supervised ViTs.

fits_no_version.finding: Pruning shrinks circuit edge fraction (32.42% dense to 12.94% at 70%) while node fraction rises (29.03% to 41.60%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In pruned ViTs, pruning produces smaller edge-count circuits that recruit a larger fraction of remaining nodes.

fits_no_version.finding: Block-11 SAE reconstruction worsens with pruning (NMSE 0.0075 dense to 0.0594 at 70%). Active SAE features rise (6,092 at 30% to 7,563 at 70%, x=32, k=128). Authors attribute this to reduced per-neuron capacity causing 'representation spreading'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reducing weight capacity spreads representations over more dictionary features, a capacity-flavoured observation not tested as a mechanism.

fits_no_version.finding: At 70% sparsity, a narrow tail of categories shows high mean-ablation scores in blocks 2 and 7.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: High pruning may concentrate some tasks onto few neurons, without a general change.

record.problems: The authors identify limitations: models are post-hoc pruned rather than trained sparse from scratch; polysemanticity and superposition are assessed with proxy measures rather than ground-truth concept annotations; experiments cover supervised ImageNet vision transformers only. Many interpretability outcomes are qualitative or shown in figures without numeric values. Circuit extraction uses a representative subset of 100 categories.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported circuit accuracy, NCQ, attribution insertion/deletion, SAE reconstruction-quality, or pruning-accuracy rows were kept because they do not directly measure the listed feature-polysemanticity versions. Figure-only values for the neuron and SAE metrics are not transcribed as numbers where the text does not state them.

untested.parts: No toy models, geometry, near-orthogonality or sparsity-dependent phase transition.
No test of whether polysemanticity stems from capacity competition, or of importance-based allocation of dedicated dimensions. Weight pruning keeps neuron count fixed.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity.
Vision transformer only; no LLM feature spread or LLM SAE recovery.
SAEs are used as probes; completeness, stability and canonicity are not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked the polysemanticity rows to V2 and gave limits_scope. But the study never manipulates or measures capacity competition, and pruning leaves dimensionality unchanged. Its premise comes from the weight-sparse-circuits literature (Gao et al.), not the capacity account. No version is tested; findings are moved to fits_no_version. Single preprint, single author, one model family.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test small toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, overlap geometry, near-orthogonality, or a sparsity-dependent geometric transition.

Tests whether pruning changes proxy measures of neuron- and SAE-feature polysemanticity, but does not identify which features receive dedicated dimensions or directly establish competition for representational capacity as the cause.
Does not test whether polysemanticity arises through a specific alternative mechanism or whether it is evidence of superposition.
Studies DeiT-III vision transformers, not LLM feature spread or LLM SAE recovery.
Uses SAEs as probes but does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of the model.
Does not test the dimensionality or geometry of the model's represented features.

rows.subject: DeiT-III B/16, dense and Wanda-pruned variants
rows.stage_stated: supervised ImageNet-1K; sparse variants fine-tuned after pruning
rows.operation_detail: Measured neuron selectivity using CLS-token activation AUROC for target classes.
rows.value: No consistent changes in selectivity across the majority of categories or sparsity levels.
rows.note: The paper gives this as an aggregate qualitative result; plotted distributions are separated by layer and sparsity, but numeric values are not stated.
rows.check: Measures the effect of weight pruning on neuron selectivity, which no version names. 'Absent' describes the pruning effect, not any version. Methods say averages use 100 categories; Section 4.2 says 1,000. Numbers are figure-only.

rows.stage_stated: supervised ImageNet-1K; sparse variants fine-tuned after pruning
rows.operation_detail: Measured neuron label entropy over class activation distributions.
rows.value: Label entropy remains high, with no consistent change across sparsity levels.
rows.note: The paper gives an aggregate qualitative result; numeric values are not stated.
rows.check: Pruning effect on neuron label entropy; no version covers this. High entropy in a ViT is not LLM evidence (V4) and says nothing about the cause (V2/V3).

rows.subject: DeiT-III B/16, Wanda 10% sparse variant
rows.operation_detail: Measured selectivity of BatchTopK SAE features.
rows.value: Higher selectivity than the dense baseline; the text describes this as an effect at 10% sparsity that does not persist at higher sparsity.
rows.check: Pruning effect on SAE-feature selectivity in a ViT. The 10% increase is described qualitatively only. 'numbers_found 1/1' is wrong, since no number is stated.

rows.value: The increase observed at 10% sparsity does not persist at higher sparsity; no systematic improvement is reported.
rows.note: The paper presents separate sparsity-level distributions in Figure 3 but does not state numeric values.
rows.check: Pruning effect on SAE selectivity at 30–70%; no version covers this.

rows.subject: DeiT-III B/16, Wanda 10% sparse variant
rows.operation_detail: Measured class variance of BatchTopK SAE features.
rows.value: Higher class variance than the dense baseline; the text says this effect does not persist at higher sparsity.
rows.check: Higher class variance means less consistent responses (lower is better per Eq. 4). So this is not an interpretability improvement, and the record conflates it with S1. No version covers it.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: DeiT-III B/16 dense and Wanda-pruned variants on ImageNet-1K
reader_labels.reason: Neuron and SAE-feature measures show no systematic reduction in polysemanticity with pruning; the reported 10% SAE selectivity and class-variance changes do not persist at higher sparsity (N1–N3, S1–S6). The study does not directly test the proposed feature-allocation mechanism.
